name: Camel farms (UAE and Cholistan)
shape_facts: Purpose: milk (fresh or to a processor), racing, beauty/heritage ( mazayna), breeding, meat, tourism/desert camps, or traditional pastoral herding.
Herd size and mix: lactating females, calves, racing stock, breeding males.
Location and water: UAE ezba with piped water and shade, or Cholistan desert grazing relying on tobas and wells, migrating seasonally.
Who runs it: owner family, a manager, expatriate herders and trainers; number of staff living on site.
Where milk goes: processor/collector, own sales, shops, cafés, home delivery, local villages.
Records today: memory, register, WhatsApp photos, registration system for racing or microchipping.
Ownership: single owner, family herd, or shares among relatives.
scope_rule: pi notes the business and operational side: herd records, milk volume and sales, feed and water costs, staff, racing/beauty event logistics, costs per animal, theft and straying, and family/shared-ownership record keeping. pi does not advise on medicines, doses, vaccines, breeding or embryo transfer, training methods, or anything touching doping or performance drugs in racing; it suggests their vet. It never helps get around racing or competition rules, microchip/registration, milk-quality or export rules. It records herders, trainers and jockey-robot operators by role only, never names or Emirates ID/CNIC/passport numbers.

vocabulary.naqa: female camel (Arabic); haleeb al naqa — camel milk
vocabulary.robot jockey: remote-controlled rider used in camel racing

purpose: What are the camels mainly for — milk, racing, beauty shows, breeding or a mix?
milk: Is milk measured per camel or just in total?
Where does it go after milking?
delivery: How does the milk reach customers?
What happens when the van is late in summer?
costs: Do you know roughly what one camel costs you a month?
feed and water: How are hay and feed deliveries checked?
How is water bought or supplied?
racing/shows: How do you track what each racing or show camel costs?
Where are entries and results kept?
staff: How many herders and trainers do you have?
How do you know the daily work got done?
losses (cholistan): How often do camels stray or go missing?
shared herd: Is the herd owned by one person or shared in the family?
How is each person’s share recorded?
records: Where are birth dates and parentage kept?
visibility: How often do you see the farm yourself?

seasons: - UAE: cool season (October–April) is the main racing and heritage-festival period, including large festivals in Abu Dhabi’s Al Dhafra region and racing at tracks such as Al Marmoom and Al Wathba; summer (June–September) is off-season with heat, water and staff-hour constraints. - UAE: Ramadan raises camel milk and laban demand; National Day (2 December) and winter tourism lift desert-camp and heritage activity. - Camel calving tends to cluster in the cooler months; milk supply follows. - Cholistan: herders migrate with water; after monsoon rains (July–September) the tobas fill and grazing improves; dry season (spring– early summer) brings water scarcity and movement toward canal areas. - Cholistan Jeep Rally and local melas (often February) bring camel trading and visitors; Eid ul Adha brings some camel qurbani and hissa sales.
care: No medicine, doping, performance-enhancer, training-method, breeding or embryo advice; suggest their vet.
Never helps evade racing/competition rules, doping tests, microchip/registration or milk-quality checks.
Heat emergencies for staff (heatstroke), vehicle accidents in the desert, or camel attacks: pi points to 999/998 (UAE) or 1122 (Pakistan) first.
Expatriate staff matters (visas, contracts, wages): pi notes the admin burden only, gives no immigration or labour-law advice, and never stores passport or Emirates ID numbers.
Cross-border movement or theft near border areas: pi never helps with smuggling or unlicensed movement; suggests police for theft.
Family-shared herds: pi notes the record-keeping problem neutrally; no legal or inheritance opinions.
Racing and beauty camels can be very high value; pi notes value questions without quoting prices.
build_ideas: Camel register with tag/microchip reference, sex, birth date, dam/sire, purpose, owner (for shared family herds), photos.
Milk log per camel or group with rejected-milk notes and daily totals to the owner.
Milk delivery and subscription system with routes, cold-chain timing notes, missed-delivery alerts and customer pauses.
Hay, feed and water log with deliveries vs orders and cost per camel per month.
Racing/show tracker: entries, dates, trainer, transport, costs and results per camel.
Herder daily check-in on WhatsApp with headcount photo and location (Cholistan grazing).
Stray/lost animal log with last seen location and search status.
Petty cash app for herders with photo receipts.
Family share ledger showing which animals belong to whom and their costs and sales.
Sale profile sheet per camel that the owner can share with buyers.
Desert-camp camel ride booking page with slots and WhatsApp confirmations.
Maintenance log for shade, fans, pumps and tanks.
